newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH sales up in 1996, DFS buy to hit EPS in 1997.
newsitem.headline: LVMH sales up in 1996, DFS buy to hit EPS in 1997.

text.p: French luxury goods conglomerate LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Thursday that its $2.6 billion acquisition of U.S. duty free chain DFS would weigh on earnings per share for 1997.

But the group is targetting higher sales and profits this year before the impact of the acquisition, LVMH said in a statement announcing a 4.6 percent rise in provisional 1996 sales to 31.14 billion francs.
It said sales rose in 1996 in its champagne and wines and designer leather goods divisions, but fell in the cognac and spirits and perfumes and beauty products divisions.
"The objective set for LVMH in 1997 is for a new increase in sales and profits before the impact of the DFS acquisition," the company said in the statement.
"The acquisition should lead to growth on the order of 50 percent for sales and close to 30 percent for LVMH's operating profit," it said.
But it said the huge acquisition would be dilutive. A spokeswoman for LVMH told Reuters the acquisition would result in lower earnings per share in 1997.
LVMH has bought 61.25 percent of DFS for around $2.6 billion after concluding a deal with the majority owners of DFS last year.
LVMH is expected to report its 1996 results on March 20.
It reported a 5.4 percent rise in its 1996 first-half net attributable profit in September and said at the time that it expected an increase in full-year profit as well.
